title: Cellular and molecular biological studies on primary human PBMCs in the context of intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia therapy (IHHT)
summary: This study investigates whether IHHT leads to changes in the blood. During IHHT, participants breathe in air with alternating levels of oxygen – some with less oxygen and some with more – through a mask. Around 30 adults who are already receiving this treatment on medical advice are eligible to take part. Participation in the study is voluntary. Over a period of 6 weeks, two to three IHHT sessions will take place each week. In addition, blood samples will be taken before the start of the study and after 2, 4 and 6 weeks. The blood samples will be analysed in the laboratory to check for any signs of changes in cell function and energy metabolism in the body. The treatment itself is not dictated by the study.

interventions.name: This is a prospective, observational study involving the collection of blood samples for the purposes of the study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants are adults who, following a medical examination, are deemed healthy enough to undergo IHHT and have received a recommendation to do so from their doctor. The medical recommendation is based on symptoms of fatigue of unknown cause. IHHT is offered as a voluntary complementary treatment. Demographic characteristics do not constitute a restriction.
Exclusion criteria:
Persons with health conditions which, in the opinion of a doctor, could prevent the IHHT from being carried out safely are excluded from taking part. These include, in particular: - acute or severe cardiovascular conditions (e.g. angina pectoris, recent heart attacks) - severe pulmonary conditions - active infections - pregnancy - other medical reasons which, in the opinion of a doctor, could compromise the safety of the IHHT.
